GOOD TO KNOW

Emails and chats are handed out differently from this release. Until now an agent who took an email stayed first in line and was given every new one until full. Now the agent holding the fewest goes first, then whoever was given one longest ago: five emails for three agents go 2, 2 and 1. Calls are shared exactly as before. Nothing needs to be changed on a queue for this.

A list belongs to a campaign through the campaign's published version. Where your organisation reviews campaign changes, moving a list takes effect when the new versions are published; with no review it is live at once.

Yaxxa AI agents need the Yaxxa AI feature on your plan and the platform's Yaxxa AI connection, with its AI model address, set up by your provider.

FOR AGENTS

Hang up while it rings: a call you place now shows Hang up from the moment you dial, not only once the customer answers. Pressing it, or Start wrap-up, stops the customer's phone ringing and ends the call.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Who gets the work first: a queue's routing now has four choices, each explained in one line on the queue's page. Longest waiting for work (the default) shares emails and chats by who holds the fewest. Least busy (new) looks at everything an agent has open across calls, chats and emails. In turn is now a true rotation per queue and channel, and an agent who was full or away keeps their place. Best skilled shares fairly between equally skilled agents. Sticky agents, reserved callbacks, skills, languages and clients still come first.

How work was shared: a new report under Reports shows, per queue, channel and agent, the items each was given beside the time they were signed in and available, with items per available hour. Agents who were available and got nothing show 0.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

AI agents on Yaxxa AI: an AI agent can now run entirely on Yaxxa AI. Choose the engine Yaxxa AI and set the three steps: Listens, Thinks and Speaks, with a voice. On a call it greets, listens, answers sentence by sentence, can be interrupted, and can transfer, end the call and use the same actions as the other engines. It also answers web chat, WhatsApp and SMS. The Test tab checks the three steps, takes a typed question and plays the reply in the agent's voice.

Import leads with a campaign: on the Upload step, Campaign (optional) gives the new list to a dialling campaign when the import completes. If the import fails, the list is not given to the campaign.

Edit list: on a list's page, Edit list changes its name and description and moves it to another campaign. The leads, their call history, outcomes and notes stay as they are. Before moving, it says what the move does and asks you to confirm when a campaign is running; when a list cannot be moved it says why, for example when it is the campaign's only list. Campaign history shows when a list was given to or moved between campaigns, and by whom. Campaign lists has a Campaign column.

Download list: a CSV of every lead in the list, not only the page on screen: details and custom columns, list and campaign, status, attempts, next retry, callback, the last call's time, number, result, outcome, agent, talk time and notes, and where each lead came from. Details a person may not see on screen are masked in the file. Choosing or changing a list's campaign needs permission to manage campaigns.

FOR PLATFORM OPERATORS

Is the trunk up?: Platform → Carriers shows each carrier as Healthy, Degraded, Down or Not checked, with the reason. Status on a carrier shows its registration, whether it answers OPTIONS and how fast, its calls now, its last answered and last failed call, and its last 20 changes, with Check now. Operators get one email when a carrier has been down for a minute and one when it is back. Where "Check the carrier is up with SIP OPTIONS" is on, the platform sends the carrier one"}
